\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پرواز} (parvāz)}{پرواز (parvāz)}]{\ur{پرواز} (parvāz) — a flight}

\label{lesson:UR-C398-parvaz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to turn (something), then the Urdu for to show (someone) around.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پرواز}}
\textbf{\ur{پرواز}} — \emph{parvāz} — \textquotedblleft{}a flight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہماری} \ur{پرواز} \ur{رات} \ur{دس} \ur{بجے} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hamārī parvāz rāt das baje hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our flight is at ten at night.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پرواز}} (\emph{parvāz}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{parvāz}, \textquotedblleft{}flying, a flight\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parvāz}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parvāz}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hamārī parvāz rāt das baje hai.} — Our flight is at ten at night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to turn (something), then the Urdu for to show (someone) around, then say \emph{parvāz} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{پرواز} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A flight\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{طیارہ} (tayyārā)}{طیارہ (tayyārā)}]{\ur{طیارہ} (tayyārā) — an aircraft}

\label{lesson:UR-C398-tayyara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to show (someone) around, then the Urdu for a flight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{طیارہ}}
\textbf{\ur{طیارہ}} — \emph{tayyārā} — \textquotedblleft{}an aircraft\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{طیارہ} \ur{بادلوں} \ur{کے} \ur{اوپر} \ur{اڑ} \ur{رہا} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tayyārā bādaloṅ ke ūpar uṛ rahā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The aircraft was flying above the clouds.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{طیارہ}} (\emph{tayyārā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ṭayyāra}, \textquotedblleft{}an aeroplane\textquotedblright{}, from a word for flying; the news prefers it to \textbf{\ur{ہوائی} \ur{جہاز}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tayyārā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tayyārā bādaloṅ ke ūpar uṛ rahā thā.} — The aircraft was flying above the clouds.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to show (someone) around, then the Urdu for a flight, then say \emph{tayyārā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نشست} (nashist)}{نشست (nashist)}]{\ur{نشست} (nashist) — a seat (formal)}

\label{lesson:UR-C398-nashist}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a flight, then the Urdu for an aircraft.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نشست}}
\textbf{\ur{نشست}} — \emph{nashist} — \textquotedblleft{}a seat (formal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میری} \ur{نشست} \ur{کھڑکی} \ur{کے} \ur{پاس} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{merī nashist khiṛkī ke pās hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My seat is by the window.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نشست}} (\emph{nashist}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{nishast}, \textquotedblleft{}a sitting, a seat\textquotedblright{}, from the verb \emph{nishastan}, \textquotedblleft{}to sit\textquotedblright{}; tickets and announcements use it where talk says \textbf{\ur{سیٹ}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nashist}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{merī nashist khiṛkī ke pās hai.} — My seat is by the window.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a flight, then the Urdu for an aircraft, then say \emph{nashist} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کسنا} (kasnā)}{کسنا (kasnā)}]{\ur{کسنا} (kasnā) — to tighten; to fasten}

\label{lesson:UR-C398-kasna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an aircraft, then the Urdu for a seat (formal).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کسنا}}
\textbf{\ur{کسنا}} — \emph{kasnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to tighten; to fasten\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{پرواز} \ur{سے} \ur{پہلے} \ur{بیلٹ} \ur{کس} \ur{لیجیے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{parvāz se pehle belṭ kas lījiye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Please fasten your seat belt before the flight.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{رسی} \ur{کسی}, \emph{us ne rassī kasī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کسنا}} (\emph{kasnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{kasnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to tighten\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{kárṣati}, \textquotedblleft{}draws, pulls\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2908).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kasnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kasnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parvāz se pehle belṭ kas lījiye.} — Please fasten your seat belt before the flight.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for an aircraft, then the Urdu for a seat (formal), then say \emph{kasnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{کسنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To tighten; to fasten\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ملتوی} (multavī)}{ملتوی (multavī)}]{\ur{ملتوی} (multavī) — postponed}

\label{lesson:UR-C398-multavi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a seat (formal), then the Urdu for to tighten.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ملتوی}}
\textbf{\ur{ملتوی}} — \emph{multavī} — \textquotedblleft{}postponed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{طوفان} \ur{کی} \ur{وجہ} \ur{سے} \ur{پرواز} \ur{ملتوی} \ur{ہو} \ur{گئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tūfān kī vajah se parvāz multavī ho gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The flight was put off because of the storm.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ملتوی}} (\emph{multavī}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{multawī}, \textquotedblleft{}turned aside, bent\textquotedblright{}; the sense \textquotedblleft{}put off till later\textquotedblright{} probably grew in Persian and Urdu.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{multavī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{multavī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tūfān kī vajah se parvāz multavī ho gaī.} — The flight was put off because of the storm.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a seat (formal), then the Urdu for to tighten, then say \emph{multavī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ملتوی} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Postponed\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
